summary: boardcraft-account owns sign-in, token resolution and single-session logout. PostgreSQL stores the salted password verifier and links each session digest to an account UUID. The in-memory client exposes a ready account only after resolving its token. Native login and secure storage, HTTP/cookie transport, protected board writes and account administration remain open in docs/workflows.md.
evidence: cargo test --locked --workspace --test account_session: both named cases passed, none ignored or filtered. Each used its own schema in the explicit rustday_test database and independent connections for readback.

rejected_credentials_then_sign_in: an unknown identifier advanced locally. Submitting it and submitting an incorrect password for the existing Viewer returned the same rejection. Empty/oversized credentials, disabled and passwordless accounts produced no session. A deferred constraint forced commit to fail; the client received no token and a fresh read still counted zero sessions.

Correction with the exact generated password succeeded. Padded mixed-case username and email lookups resolved the same read-only Viewer UUID. Independent reads verified the salted PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 password verifier and matched the SHA-256 digest of each encoded 32-byte bearer to its committed account link.

resolve_retry_and_revoke: making the fixture role column unavailable prevented readiness after issuance and again on token-only reopen. Restoring the column allowed retry without credentials. A separate role update then resolved as Member under the same UUID. Two logins issued distinct tokens; logout removed only the first digest. Reopen with the revoked token cleared it, the other session still resolved, and disabling the account made that client clear its token on resume.

Coordinator comparison: the reference login component using a disposable account operation and in-memory request adapter advanced unknown, whitespace-only and oversized nonempty identifiers without an existence or format check. The password step rejected each like a wrong password and kept retry available. The resolved Viewer, role refresh after a connection failure, and single-token logout with a rejected cold resume matched the Rust client and independent database readbacks. No browser cookie, native window or board mutation was exercised.

A fresh Astra 6.2 High worker ran through the runner. Runner verified 13-account-session after workspace formatting, both required cases and all 13 portable workspace tests passed. The 16 runner regressions passed separately, as did account-crate Clippy for all targets with warnings denied.
next: Gate authenticated loopback requests: resolve the session at the host and prove a Viewer rename is denied without changing the stored board.
